In Chile's Atacama Desert, light rain occurs on average about once every few years. But when enough moisture reaches the ground, more than 200 species of flowers, including the añañuca, can bloom in one of the driest places in the world. This year, heavy rains brought on by El Niño led the Atacama to erupt into a sea of colorful blooms.
